title: Theophylact Simocatta, Letters (Ἐπιστολαὶ ἠθικαί, ἀγροικικαί, ἑταιρικαί): 85 fictional letters / Феофилакт Симокатта, Письма
author: Theophylact Simocatta
size: 85 letters; about 7,500–8,000 words (my estimate from Hercher's text)
edition: Zanetto, Teubner 1985. Public domain: Hercher, Epistolographi Graeci (1873), archive.org. Copernicus' Latin version of 1509.
ru_evidence: 19 of 85 letters (I–V, XV, XIX–XXI, XXXIV, XXXVIII–XL, L, LI, LXI, LXXXIII–LXXXV) translated by T. A. Miller in Памятники византийской литературы IV–IX вв. (1968), pp. 244–249; online at myriobiblion.byzantion.ru/feofilact.htm
en_evidence: No English translation found. English Wikipedia lists only Copernicus' Latin (1509); a BMCR search shows none. The work is not on romanletters.org.
other_translations: Latin: Copernicus 1509 (reprinted Hipler 1873). Modern-language translations: none found (unverified).
value: The last flowering of the Alciphron/Aelian fictional-letter genre, bridging the Second Sophistic and Byzantium. Copernicus' only self-published book was its translation. Appeals to historians of literature and science and to general readers.
ai_feasibility: High. Short, self-contained, mannered prose; the mythological and proverbial allusions are easy to annotate. Can be completed and fully reviewed quickly.
pilot_unit: The whole collection (85 letters, about 8,000 words), an ideal first complete publication.
